title: Real-time output and external-action interoperability certification for onboarded models
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Certify that newly onboarded model variants can be pinned to customer workloads while delivering correct, low-latency streaming outputs and deterministic external-action (function/tool) invocation semantics. This ticket covers verification automation, documentation updates, and publishing of a model performance profile used by routing and billing tiers.

Background: As we onboard wider model families and richer function-calling semantics, customers rely on stable version pinning and accurate performance expectations. Several regressions were observed last quarter where a model change altered chunking behavior and caused tool invocations to be reordered under backpressure. We need a repeatable certification path that exercises real-time output paths, KV/prefix cache interactions, batching, sequence-splitting, and function-call event ordering across pinned versions.

Scope:
- Build an automated interoperability test harness that runs streamed conversations against each onboarding candidate and a suite of external-tool mocks (HTTP webhooks, Redis queues, and our internal tool proxy).
- Validate ordering, latency, and payload fidelity of function/tool invocations under normal, burst, and degraded network conditions.
- Generate a publishable "performance profile" artifact capturing median/95/99 latency, tokens/sec throughput, memory footprint, and observed chunk sizes under canonical prompt mixes.
- Add gating checks to the onboarding pipeline so a model cannot be promoted to pinned status unless compatibility tests pass.
- Produce a short runbook for Ops/SEs on interpreting the profile and recommended fallback pins for SLAs.

Out of scope: exhaustive adversarial fuzzing of tooling protocols, changes to downstream SDKs (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria:
- Automated harness runs end-to-end against model candidate and reports pass/fail.
- Function/tool invocation ordering is stable in 1000 sample conversations across three simulated network conditions.
- Latency and throughput metrics are published to the model registry as a performance profile JSON.
- Onboarding pipeline rejects candidate if any critical interop assertion fails.
- Documentation and runbook published and linked from model onboarding playbook.
test_plan: Create canonical convo set (golden prompts) covering: simple tool call, nested tool call suggestions, interleaved streaming text + tool triggers, and long-context resumption.
Implement tool mocks: webhook echo server, redis-queue consumer that asserts ordering, and internal tool-proxy stub with configurable delay/drop behavior.
Run harness under three network conditions: stable (no delay), moderate jitter (50-200ms), high latency/loss (200-800ms, 1% drop).
Measure: message ordering violations, tool payload diffs (schema/extra fields), token-level latency (generate-to-first-tool-event), and end-to-end completion time percentiles.

Regression threshold: ordering violations = 0 in stable; <= 1 per 1000 conversations in moderate; <= 2 per 1000 in high latency. Latency regressions flagged if 95p increases >25% from baseline profile.
Integrate one-off manual exploratory run with real partner dataset (with partner consent) before final sign-off.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge harness and tests behind feature flag and run nightly against staging model snapshots. 2) Run full certification for the candidate model and generate profile artifact. 3) Publish profile to model registry and mark candidate as pin-eligible. 4) Canary: enable pinned routing for 5% of traffic with detailed tracing enabled for 48 hours. 5) If no regressions, escalate pin to 100% for customers that requested it. 6) Notify SDK/Docs teams to update stability notes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Test harness may not reproduce complex production tool proxies. Mitigation: provide an extensible plugin interface for third-party tool simulators and require partner-side quick smoke tests.
Risk: Publishing inaccurate profiles could mislead customers. Mitigation: use conservative quantiles (median and 99p) and flag profiles as 'preliminary' until canary completes.

Risk: Enforcement could block good models due to flaky network tests. Mitigation: isolate deterministic assertions (ordering/payload) from flaky latency assertions and require human review for flaky failures.
Risk: Increased CI cost/time. Mitigation: run heavy workloads in nightly batch; keep fast sanity checks in the pre-merge pipeline.
